result.answer:
In Minimi 2.0 (launched September 24, 2026), the two AI cats split the work: **Cotton remembers, and Melody chases commitments.**

- **Cotton** — the memory side. It's the original cat (Minimi 1.0 was billed as "Your Ambient Memory layer for Claude"), and in 2.0 it's the one "who remembers" — personal context captured on your Mac [S5](https://chatgate.ai/en/post/minimi-2-0#1). Minimi's own site frames this as memory that "lives on your Mac, where it's safest," claiming 54% vs. 36% prior state of the art on the BEAM long-term memory benchmark [S12](https://www.projectminimi.com/memory).
- **Melody** — the follow-through side, introduced in 2.0 as "the Closer": it tracks down open loops such as promises made in chat channels and overlooked follow-ups, and per the launch framing "never lets you miss your commitments" [S27](https://coding4food.com/en/post/minimi-2-0-can-cute-ai-cats-solve-context-switching-nightmare) [S5](https://chatgate.ai/en/post/minimi-2-0#1).

One caveat on sourcing: the clearest descriptions of the Cotton/Melody split come from launch coverage and the Product Hunt listing as reported by third parties, not from a dedicated feature page on projectminimi.com — the official site page I found covers the memory capability rather than naming both cats [S12](https://www.projectminimi.com/memory).

result.answer:
**No — per the vendor's own description, Minimi does not take screenshots.** It reads what's on your Mac screen through macOS **Accessibility** APIs instead of capturing images.

**Cotton's role:** Cotton is the memory side of Minimi 2.0 — it accumulates the context of what you read, hear, and do on your Mac into a private, on-device memory layer (Melody, the other character, tracks unfinished commitments) [S5](https://www.nextfor.ai/products/minimi-2-0-2), [S9](https://chatgate.ai/en/post/minimi-2-0#1).

**How it reads the screen:** A review of the product states that the official site says it reads screen content via macOS Accessibility rather than screenshots; microphone and system-audio capture require separate permissions, and the policy notes that recording other people's conversations requires any legally required consent [S8](https://aitrovex.com/zh-hans/tool/minimi). Memories are stored as embeddings in a local vector database on your Mac, and the company says nothing is kept on its servers or used for training [S5](https://www.nextfor.ai/products/minimi-2-0-2), [S2](https://www.projectminimi.com/memory).

Two caveats:
- The Accessibility-vs-screenshot wording comes from a third-party summary of the site, not a direct quote from the vendor page I retrieved; the official memory page I checked only says memory stays on your Mac and that it uses "the same permissions as WisprFlow" [S2](https://www.projectminimi.com/memory).
- The search digest was truncated, so I can't rule out that the site elsewhere mentions optional screenshot-based features.

**Sources**
- [S2](https://www.projectminimi.com/memory) — minimi memory page
- [S5](https://www.nextfor.ai/products/minimi-2-0-2) — minimi 2.0 features overview
- [S8](https://aitrovex.com/zh-hans/tool/minimi) — aitrovex product summary (Accessibility vs. screenshots)
- [S9](https://chatgate.ai/en/post/minimi-2-0#1) — chatgate.ai on minimi 2.0

result.answer:
**What stays on your Mac:** your memory — the index of your activity — is kept in a local vector database on the device, and Minimi's own copy says "Your memory lives on your Mac, where it's safest" [S2](https://www.projectminimi.com/memory). A launch write-up of the privacy copy (updated 2026-08-12) likewise says memory stays on your Mac [S7](https://sudoai.net/launches/minimi/#main-content). Third-party summaries describe the same design: data is stored in a local vector database, decrypted only at retrieval time and re-encrypted afterwards, so the main index never leaves the device, with per-app indexing toggles and a global pause [S8](https://www.aitoolnet.com/ru/minimi#1), [S15](https://www.aitoolnet.com/minimi#1).

**What creates embeddings:** Google's **Gemini API**, on a **paid tier**. Minimi uses the paid Gemini API tier to generate embeddings, which the write-up says ensures the processed data isn't used to train the provider's models [S15](https://www.aitoolnet.com/minimi#1), [S8](https://www.aitoolnet.com/ru/minimi#1).

So the honest framing is: the *memory store* is local, but embedding generation is a cloud call to Gemini — that's the seam in the privacy story, and a competitor's docs explicitly frame it as Minimi's "privacy gap" versus cloud-free embeddings [S14](https://heypace.app/docs/knowledge/competitive/project-minimi-rag-snapshot/).

Caveat: the Gemini detail comes from third-party tool directories (June 2026), not from Minimi's own privacy page in the digest, so treat the exact tier wording as second-hand.

result.answer:
**The two scores:** Minimi 54% vs. LIGHT (BEAM) 36%, measured on BEAM, the ICLR 2026 benchmark for long-term memory [S2](https://www.projectminimi.com/memory).

**What the 50% means:** It's a relative improvement over the previous state of the art, not a 50-point gap. 54 ÷ 36 = 1.5, so Minimi's score is 50% higher than LIGHT's — the absolute difference is 18 percentage points [S2](https://www.projectminimi.com/memory). Minimi's own framing is "50% more accurate than previous SOTA" [S2](https://www.projectminimi.com/memory), echoed in its launch material ("beat the published benchmark of 0.36 (BEAM) by 50%") [S4](https://www.producthunt.com/p/shram/minimi-3).

Two caveats worth noting: the claim is a vendor self-report, and third-party write-ups note that the underlying evaluation details (harness, dataset split, scoring method) aren't published alongside the headline number [S9](https://ustack.app/products/minimi). Also, "54% accurate" is a low absolute score — the 50% figure is flattering precisely because the baseline is low.

**Sources**
- [S2](https://www.projectminimi.com/memory) — Minimi memory page (54% vs 36%, BEAM ICLR 2026)
- [S4](https://www.producthunt.com/p/shram/minimi-3) — Product Hunt launch thread
- [S9](https://ustack.app/products/minimi) — ustack.app product listing (notes limited evaluation detail)
